_comment: Direction scales for Jev Score questions, level 0..4 (0 = 'low' pole, 4 = 'high' pole). Hand-written scales: haredi_draft, judicial, sovereignty, religion_state. Others use the generic template from `poles` (scripts/jev_direction.py). `issue_axis` maps issue ids (manual/issue_defs.json) to an axis.

haredi_draft.instructions: Assume the Israeli bill in `bill_title_hebrew` concerns military service obligations (including of Haredi yeshiva students). Which way does it push?
criteria: Strongly protects or entrenches draft exemptions for yeshiva students (e.g. enshrines Torah study as equal to service)
Somewhat eases or regulates exemptions in a way that keeps most yeshiva students out of service
Neutral, procedural, or unrelated to who must serve
Somewhat increases the service obligation or encourages service (incentives, recruiting duties, conditioning positions on service)
Strongly enforces conscription: sanctions on draft evaders and their institutions, cutting benefits or rights from those who do not serve, mandatory service for all
haredi_draft.topic: military service obligations, including the draft of Haredi yeshiva students

judicial.instructions: Assume the Israeli bill in `bill_title_hebrew` concerns the courts, judges, the Attorney General or legal advisers. Which way does it shift power?
criteria: Strongly protects judicial independence or the independence of the Attorney General and legal advisers
Somewhat strengthens judicial or legal-adviser independence
Neutral, technical, or does not shift power between elected officials and the legal system
Somewhat increases the power of the government or Knesset over courts or legal advisers
Strongly increases political control: override clause, politicians choosing judges, splitting or weakening the Attorney General, limiting judicial review
judicial._note: A mechanism-only wording ('ignore how the bill justifies itself') was tested 2026-10-11 and did worse (15/21 title-only, 11/21 with text).
judicial.topic: the power balance between elected politicians and the courts, the Attorney General, prosecutors or legal advisers

sovereignty.instructions: Assume the Israeli bill in `bill_title_hebrew` concerns the status of Judea and Samaria (the West Bank) or areas in it. Which way does it push?
criteria: Strongly blocks or reverses Israeli control or annexation
Makes annexation harder (e.g. requires a referendum or special majority)
Neutral or procedural
Somewhat expands Israeli civilian control or settlement
Applies Israeli sovereignty (annexation) to Judea and Samaria, the Jordan Valley or a settlement
sovereignty.topic: the status of Judea and Samaria (the West Bank): annexation, settlement and Israeli control

religion_state.instructions: Assume the Israeli bill in `bill_title_hebrew` concerns religion and state: marriage, Shabbat, kashrut, conversion, the Chief Rabbinate or rabbinical courts. Which way does it push?
criteria: Strongly liberal or pluralist: civil marriage, public transport on Shabbat, ending the rabbinate's monopoly (kashrut competition, private conversion), narrowing rabbinical court jurisdiction
Somewhat liberal: eases a religious restriction, adds public or non-Orthodox representation in religious bodies, limits rabbinic powers
Neutral, procedural or budgetary with no clear direction
Somewhat increases religious authority: more powers or budget for the rabbinate or religious councils, religious rules in public institutions
Strongly increases religious authority: extends rabbinical court jurisdiction, cancels the kashrut reform, bans or penalties based on Jewish religious law
religion_state.topic: religion and state: marriage, Shabbat, kashrut, conversion, the Chief Rabbinate and rabbinical courts
